description:
The Backward (BDF2) time scheme is not delivering second-order accuracy, because the Rhie-Chow ddtCorr is hardcoded Euler while rAU picks up BDF2's 1.5V/dt diagonal. The two are inconsistent by a factor tending to 1.5 as dt -> 0.

ALL THREE PIECES, from source (verified 2026-08-07):

1. BDF2 coefficients -- crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/schemes.rs:126-131
       mat.ldu.diag[c] += 1.5 * v / dt;
       mat.source[c]   += (u_old.internal[c] * 2.0 - u_oo.internal[c] * 0.5) * (v / dt);

2. ddt_corr is hardcoded Euler regardless of scheme -- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvc/ddt_corr.rs:58-74. It takes NO scheme argument: `let r_dt = 1.0 / dt;` (:67), `coeff * phi_corr * r_dt` (:73). Its own doc (:28, :53-57) says "Rhie-Chow time-derivative flux correction (Euler scheme) ... Mirrors EulerDdtScheme<Type>::fvcDdtPhiCorr".

3. rAU picks up the BDF2 diagonal -- crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/pimple_foam/mod.rs:394-412. u_eqn = ddt_term + div_term + ... (:394); let a = u_eqn.a_field() (:397), and a_field() returns the raw diagonal (crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/ldu_matrix/fv_vector_matrix.rs:109-121); then mesh.cell_volumes[c] / a_data[c] (:401). With Backward selected that diagonal contains 1.5*V/dt. The two are combined at :430-431 (rauf = fvc::interpolate(&rau); ddt_corr = fvc::ddt_corr(&u_old, &phi_old, dt)) and added to phiHbyA at :462.

NO ORDER-OF-ACCURACY TEST EXISTS for any ddt scheme. The only two Backward tests are:
- schemes.rs:275 backward_ddt_matches_the_bdf2_formula -- asserts COEFFICIENTS only (diag = 15, source_x = 35 at dt = 0.1), plus Euler fallback on start-up and SteadyState = zero. Algebra check, not a temporal convergence study.
- crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/tests/fv_scheme_selection.rs:342 backward_ddt_selection_is_live_and_not_worse_against_ghia -- asserts only that the run stays finite, that the selection is live (d_transient > 1e-9), and rms_b <= rms_e + 1e-4 with rms_b < 0.10. Its own doc (:338-341) says it "deliberately does not assert steady-state equivalence, because that is currently false."

MEASURED (re-ran cargo test --release --test fv_scheme_selection backward_ddt_selection):
    max |U_backward - U_euler|: transient (5 steps) = 2.829482e-2 m/s, long-time (12 s) = 1.649884e-2 m/s
    Ghia Re=100 centreline RMS at 12 s: Euler 0.0363, Backward 0.0359
This matches the dt = 4e-3 row of the doc table exactly.

HONESTY CAVEAT: the dt sweep at fv_scheme_selection.rs:303-308 (1.0394e-2 @ 8e-3 -> 2.9258e-2 @ 1e-3, i.e. the discrepancy GROWS as dt is refined -- the signature of an order-inconsistency) is a DOC-COMMENT RECORD of a manual sweep. The shipped test runs only dt = 4e-3 and asserts nothing about the trend. Only the 4e-3 row is reproducible from the tree today.

WORK:
1. Give fvc::ddt_corr a scheme argument so it matches the selected ddt scheme (OpenFOAM has backwardDdtScheme::fvcDdtPhiCorr for exactly this).
2. Add a temporal order-of-accuracy test (manufactured solution or Taylor-Green) that measures observed order and asserts ~2 for Backward and ~1 for Euler. The workspace V&V rule requires the measured result to be recorded in the test's doc comment.
3. Re-run the dt sweep under test so the rows at 8e-3/2e-3/1e-3 stop being doc-only.
title: outram-foam: Backward (BDF2) is not 2nd-order — ddtCorr is Euler-only while rAU uses 1.5V/dt

description: FOUNDATION for the polyhedral-volume-mesh roadmap. Take a closed watertight surface (the crate's current output) and fill its interior with a tetrahedral volume mesh via constrained/conforming Delaunay tetrahedralization (pure-Rust, TetGen-like: Bowyer-Watson insertion + boundary recovery + quality/size refinement, Shewchuk predicates already in boolean_predicates). This is the prerequisite for polyhedral cells, boundary layers, and real volume polyMesh export. ARCHITECTURE DECISION PENDING: host in outram-blender (a new volume module set) vs a new sibling crate (e.g. outram-mesh-gen) that outram-blender drives. Education/research/V&V only per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md. V&V: tetrahedralize a cube/sphere, assert positive-volume tets, boundary faces == input surface, sum(tet vols)==enclosed volume.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: ARCH FINDING (2026-07-24 survey): outram-foam-basic-lib already provides the mesh REPRESENTATION + FV addressing (mesh/fv_mesh.rs FvMesh: cells/owner/neighbour/volumes/centres/areas/patches+validate; io/poly_mesh.rs PolyMesh: read/write/to_fv_mesh/total_volume) and genfoam has mesh_to_mesh region mapping — but NO generation (no blockMesh/snappy/tet/Delaunay/dual/boundary-layer). So the new outram-mesh-gen crate is confirmed: it CONSUMES an outram-blender surface Mesh, GENERATES tet->polyhedral cells (+prism layers), and EMITS a foam PolyMesh; foam's existing to_fv_mesh()/write() make it solvable/writable. Do NOT reinvent FvMesh. op-hzs.35 (volume polyMesh export) is therefore: produce a real-cell PolyMesh targeting outram-foam-basic-lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: PROVENANCE/LICENSING (per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md + GPLv3 rule): the reference tet mesher TetGen (Hang Si) is AGPL and CGAL parts are GPL/commercial — implement CLEAN-ROOM from PUBLISHED ALGORITHMS/PAPERS only, do NOT port TetGen/CGAL code. Key references to source: Si 'TetGen, a Delaunay-Based Quality Tetrahedral Mesh Generator' (ACM TOMS 2015); Shewchuk 'Constrained Delaunay Tetrahedralizations and Provably Good Boundary Recovery' (2002) + 'Tetrahedral Mesh Generation by Delaunay Refinement' (1998); Cheng/Dey/Shewchuk 'Delaunay Mesh Generation' (book). Polyhedral dual + boundary layers: OpenFOAM polyDualMesh + snappyHexMesh addLayers (GPLv3, reference-clean).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: DECISION SUPERSEDES the clean-room-TetGen note above (2026-07-24): do NOT use TetGen (AGPL) and do NOT build a from-scratch Delaunay mesher. Instead PORT cfMesh (GPL-3.0, https://github.com/wyldckat/cfMesh) into the new crate crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh (scaffold landed, commit db924dd), with voro++ (modified-BSD, LBNL, https://github.com/chr1shr/voro) as the Voronoi/polyhedral-dual reference. Both vendored gitignored under upstream_source/{cfMesh@6cf1d21, voro@b0dac57}. op-hzs.32/.33/.34/.35 are now PORT tasks (cfMesh tetMesh/cartesianMesh -> polyhedral dual via voro++ -> boundaryLayers -> foam PolyMesh), not from-scratch algorithm builds. Crate consumes outram-blender Mesh, emits outram-foam-basic-lib PolyMesh.

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model**

Required for hydroprocessing, and **the key acceptance case for the
flowsheet solver** because it introduces a genuine recycle/tear stream.

```
reactor effluent -> HP separator -> H2-rich gas -> acid-gas cleanup
                                                -> compressor
                                                -> back to reactor inlet
```

**The steady-state solver must converge the recycle without hand iteration by
the user.** If a user has to manually iterate a tear stream, the solver's
recycle handling is not usable and that is the finding.

Audit the existing `flowsheet_solver` recycle/tear machinery first -- 11 files
exist there and the capability may already be present but unexposed.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Hydrogen recycle

description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 07:10 (filed outside active hours -- no ingestion or code work done yet).

Source: https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/4152287

Requested work, in order:
1. INGEST the PDF into kovan (HARD RULE: any literature used goes into crates/kovan-literature, catalogued, with access tier and provenance).
   - Stage the PDF in kovan_import/ (gitignored) first.
   - Decide the ACCESS TIER from the document's own copyright page, NOT from the fact that OSTI hosts it publicly. OSTI hosting grants no redistribution rights by itself; if unsure, treat as proprietary.
   - kovan lit import <pdf> --json-out ... --markdown-out ... ; then check the extracted metadata (it is frequently wrong -- title/author/year failures are common) and confirm kovan lit bibtex round-trips cleanly.
   - Watch for a text-and-data-mining / AI-training reservation in the copyright line (see op-b7bx); if present, catalogue metadata + factual findings only, do not extract full text.
   - Update crates/kovan-literature/CATALOGUE.md.
   - Delete the staged copy once catalogued.
2. UPDATE the TUAS conduction/material-property libraries with the data from this document.
   - Search-before-building rule applies: check tuas_boussinesq_solver's existing SolidMaterial correlations, outram-park-fork-offbeat's ~70 material correlations, and the foam/tampines solid-thermo layers BEFORE adding anything new. Extend in place where a correlation already exists.
   - Cite the kovan catalogue entry in the doc comment of every correlation added or changed, with the stated validity temperature range.
3. USE it accordingly in the downstream models (htgr_sim_v1 / HTR-10 components) once the properties exist.

Note: the document contents have NOT been read yet, so the exact steels/properties it covers are unconfirmed -- confirm on ingestion before scoping step 2.

Related: op-x0v1 (steel properties valid to 1200 C) -- this may be the data source for it.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
Second source added by maintainer, 2026-08-13 07:1x (still outside active hours; not yet fetched or read):

Access-tier note: NIST publications are OFTEN US-Government works and therefore public domain, but this must be CONFIRMED from the document itself -- NIST also republishes third-party copyrighted material, and the hosting domain is not evidence of tier. If the two sources disagree on a property value, record both in the correlation's doc comment with their respective citations rather than silently picking one.
